source.title: Red Alert: Shadow Fleet Sanctions Evasion and Avoidance Network

summary: A JMLIT+ Red Alert (ref 0774-NECC, July 2025) jointly issued by the NCA, OFSI and FCDO warns that a resilient network split into 'blue' (Western-facing) and 'red' (Russia-facing) sides trades Russian oil, led on the blue side by UK-sanctioned 2RIVERS DMCC and 2RIVERS PTE and on the red side by UK-sanctioned NORD AXIS, to evade sanctions. The network is run by UK-sanctioned Azeris Etibar EYYUB and Tahir GARAYEV, who have personal ties to UK-sanctioned ROSNEFT CEO Igor SECHIN giving privileged access to Russian oil. It uses over 100 aging Shadow Fleet tankers employing AIS switch-off, ship-to-ship transfers and flag changes, plus transhipment and mixing operations and easily replaceable front companies, to obscure Russian origin and access Western finance, insurance and trading platforms. The alert lists red flag indicators and asks firms to file SARs or report to OFSI.

citations.quote: The 2RIVERS network utilises over 100 Shadow Fleet oil tankers, vessels which are usually over 15 years old and use deceptive shipping practices to carry Russian oil.

Deceptive practices include switching off the ship's automatic identification system (AIS) to avoid the ship's movements being tracked, engaging in ship-to-ship transfers to obscure the origin of the oil before it reaches its destination, and regularly changing flags.
with deliberately obscure ownership structures and many front companies designed to be replaced with ease if they are subject to Western sanctions, trades Russian oil directly

the people behind it will likely continue to attempt to manipulate the system to benefit their trade by replacing sanctioned entities with freshly incorporated companies clean of sanctions but fulfilling the same role
Money and oil move between the companies through transhipments of oil and mixing operations to hide the Russian origin.

This company moves it on a Shadow Fleet vessel to a terminal in a third-party location, the refined product is “sold” to another company within the same network which then sells the oil on the open market to the ultimate customer who may have no sight of its Russian origins.
This “blue” company is able to benefit from all of the Western services but still acquire and sell Russian oil at favourable prices.

Access to Western rates of trade finance, trusted insurers and key commodity exchanges utilised by ‘blue’ companies are combined with the special relationship with ROSNEFT’s CEO and privileged access to Russian oil of the ‘red’ companies, to create a global trading network generating billions of USD.

extraction_notes: Alert reference 0774-NECC v1.0, jointly issued by NCA, OFSI and FCDO under JMLIT+. 'Blue' and 'red' sides of the network are extracted as category actors since the document describes them as a structural split rather than naming a single legal entity for each; individual member companies beyond 2RIVERS DMCC/PTE and NORD AXIS are referenced only as 'many more companies within this network' (p.4) and not named. Jurisdictions list is necessarily partial: the document also references 'the Global West', a 'third-party location' and unnamed 'high-risk jurisdictions' generically (pp.3-5) without naming countries, and the EU (mentioned p.3 as a sanctioning body) has no ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code so is omitted. Four typologies proposed to the Knowledge Centre (SAN002 Shadow Fleet, SAN004 Front Companies, SAN003 Transshipment, TBML010 Sanctions Evasion Through Trade); no emergent typology was needed as the library covered every technique described. TBML010 confidence set medium rather than high because the document does not use trade-finance-specific language (invoicing, documentation) beyond describing the commercial chain itself.
